lesson.title: Le Train, Le Billet & La Gare
lesson.subtitle: Navigating the SNCF: le train, le billet, la gare, réservations, and platforms.

hook.title: At the Train Station: Le Train, Le Billet & La Gare
hook.content: Just as you 'take' a coffee with prendre (Je prends un café), you ALSO 'take' the train, bus, or metro with prendre: Je prends le train à la gare ('I take the train at the station')! And your ticket is le billet (/bijɛ/).

footnotes.title: Why French has both 'le billet' (train/plane ticket) and 'le ticket' (metro/bus slip)
footnotes.content: For a reserved journey on a train or plane (or a €20 banknote!), French says un billet.

pattern.title: prendre le train + avoir son billet + attendre à la gare
pattern.content: Combine station vocabulary with your verb engines.
pattern.linguist_note: Transport expressions in French use transitive prendre ('take') + definite article (prendre le train).
pattern.trap_note: Remember: j'attends le train ('I am waiting for the train') needs NO preposition 'for'!

exercises.prompt: Match each station word or phrase with its meaning:
exercises.target_answer: the train station, the train, the (train) ticket, to take the train, to wait for the train
exercises.meaning: la gare, le train, le billet (de train), prendre le train, attendre le train
exercises.explanation: prendre le train and attendre le train both take direct objects.

exercises.prompt: How do you say 'I am taking the train at eight o'clock'?
options: J'ai le train à huit heures
Je prends le train à huit heures
Je prends du train à huit heures
exercises.target_answer: Je prends le train à huit heures
exercises.meaning: I take the train at eight o'clock
exercises.explanation: Modes of transport with prendre use the definite article: Je prends le train.

exercises.prompt: Write 'my train ticket' using 'mon billet' + 'de train':
exercises.english_hint: no article after de for type of ticket
exercises.explanation: un billet de train = 'a train ticket'.

exercises.idea: I have my ticket and I am waiting for the train at the station
cues: I have my ticket → J'ai mon billet
and I wait-for the train at the station → et j'attends le train à la gare
idea_parts: waiting + location → et j'attends le train à la gare
exercises.target_answer: J'ai mon billet et j'attends le train à la gare
exercises.meaning: I have my ticket and I'm waiting for the train at the station

diagnosis.cue: attendre already means 'to wait for': j'attends le train.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: À quelle heure est-ce que tu prends le train
exercises.target_answer: À quelle heure est-ce que tu prends le train
exercises.meaning: At what time are you taking the train?
cues: est-ce que tu prends le train
exercises.affirmation: You wrote À quelle heure and tu prends le train cleanly.

summary.outcome: Navigate train stations using la gare, le train, le billet, prendre le train, and attendre le train.

use_example.german: Je vais à la gare parce que je prends le train de midi.
use_example.english: I'm going to the station because I'm taking the noon train.

summary.takeaway: You 'take' both coffee and trains with prendre: Je prends un café, je prends le train.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on Le Pont ([5132] Départ, Arrivée & Aller-Retour): see how Le Train, Le Billet & La Gare leads directly into Départ, Arrivée & Aller-Retour.

twist.prompt: Think it through again without looking back — express "I have my ticket and I'm waiting for the train at the station" in French:
twist.target_answer: J'ai mon billet et j'attends le train à la gare
twist.explanation: Re-constructing "J'ai mon billet et j'attends le train à la gare" from the underlying rule cements the pattern of Le Train, Le Billet & La Gare.

train.context_phrase: Le train part à huit heures.
train.etymology_derivation: Old French traïn 'a line of things pulled along'.

billet.etymology_derivation: Double ll after i sounds like /j/.

gare.etymology_derivation: Originally a river shelter where boats pulled in.

réservation.etymology_derivation: English wrote the accent out; French kept the é so you know where the stress lands.

attendre.context_translation: I am waiting for the train.
attendre.etymology_derivation: Latin attendere 'to stretch toward'. In French it means to wait for — with no preposition 'for' needed!

heure.etymology_derivation: Latin hōra. Silent H triggers elision: l'heure.

quand.etymology_derivation: Latin quandō. In liaison before a vowel, the d sounds like /t/: quand il arrive /kɑ̃.t‿il/.
